paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. When God's Word is found, it is meant to be heard, and hearing it should move you. Josiah heard the Book of the Law and he tore his clothes (2 Kings 22:11). He didn't file it under "interesting reading." I once got a warning label in the mail and tossed it in a drawer, and you know how well that went for me.

Now look at WHO Josiah is. He could have pointed a finger at his fathers and said it was their mess, but he says the LORD's wrath burns against "us" (2 Kings 22:13). Then the LORD tells him, "because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD… I have heard you" (2 Kings 22:19). Humbling yourself is not a show for the neighbors. The LORD hears a tender heart, and He says so.

Here's what that means for you, baker. The same Book is open in front of you, and the question is what you do when you hear it. Don't just nod and move on. Let it get to your heart, then go and ask the LORD like Josiah did (2 Kings 22:13). And the LORD's word to Josiah was not the end of the story, so keep your ovens warm.
